extracted.intended_audience: students and technicians in clinical/microbiology laboratories
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural guidelines and quality requirements for preparing, sterilising, inoculating, and incubating bacteriological culture media and for operating incubators and thermo-regulators. Includes recipes, sterilisation schedules, aseptic technique, and media-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start from standard nutrient base
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare specialised media by beginning with the standard nutrient gelatine or nutrient agar procedures (referenced sections) and measure out the specified volume (commonly 1000 c.c.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recipes instruct 'Prepare nutrient gelatine (_vide_ page 164)' or 'Prepare nutrient agar (_vide_ page 167)' and then modify; always follow the base protocol exactly before adding special ingredients or adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additives: specified concentrations and allowable alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Add chemical additives at the stated weights/percentages (e.g., carbolic acid 5 g = 0.5%; alternatives 1 g or 2.5 g = 0.1% or 0.25% may be used to meet special requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the listed gramme amounts and note parenthetical percentage equivalents; where alternatives are given, use them only for special purposes and document the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration when necessary (papier Chardin / Swedish filter paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter media 'if necessary' through papier Chardin or through Swedish filter paper as specified for clarity and removal of precipitates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hot-water funnel when filtering hot agar; choose filter type per recipe (papier Chardin for many agars, Swedish filter paper for certain decoctions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tube and sterilise 'as for' nutrient gelatine/agar
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparation and additions, transfer media into tubes and sterilise using the same sterilisation method stated for nutrient gelatine or nutrient agar (commonly fractional/steam sterilisation schedules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many recipes abbreviate this as 'Tube, and sterilise as for nutrient agar/gelatine'—ensure you apply the full sterilisation schedule from the referenced base protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Steaming at 100°C to dissolve peptone and precipitate phosphates
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat mixtures in the steamer at 100°C for specified times (e.g., 30 minutes to dissolve peptone; 20 minutes subsequently to precipitate phosphates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the exact times given (30 min, 20 min depending on step) and follow with filtration where instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutralisation / reaction adjustment to indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjust the reaction (pH) of the medium to the specified value, often by adding decinormal soda, normal caustic soda, phosphoric acid, or other reagents, and check against litmus or phenolphthalein as specified (examples: render reaction -5, +3, +10, +13, +15, +25, 0, neutral to litmus paper).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutralise carefully by successive small additions; use the indicator specified (litmus, phenolphthalein) and re-check after heating steps since reaction can change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sterile litmus solution for colouring
rubrics_metrics.description: Add sterile litmus solution to the medium to produce the specified tint (e.g., deep lavender, deep purple, pale lavender) for litmus media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colour serves as an indicator of reaction; add only sterile litmus and in amounts sufficient to reach the described tint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification with egg when indicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify certain media (gelatine and agar) with egg (egg-white clarification) when instructed (e.g., cool to below 60°C and clarify with egg as for nutrient agar/gelatine).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cool to specified temperature before clarifying; follow the base clarifying procedure referenced (e.g., 'as for nutrient agar').

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific glycerine percentages for glycerinated media
rubrics_metrics.description: Add glycerine in the stated percentages for glycerinated media (e.g., glycerine bouillon/agar 6% for tubercle bacillus media; glycerine blood-serum usually 5%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different glycerine percentages (4–8%) are used for special purposes; 5% is commonly used for blood-serum media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potato decoction preparation and resting time
rubrics_metrics.description: For potato-based media, wash, peel, grate potatoes, weigh gratings, add distilled water in proportion of 1 c.c. per gramme weight, and allow to stand in the ice-chest for twelve hours before straining and filtering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe 12-hour cold maceration to extract potato constituents; strain through butter muslin then filter through Swedish filter paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glycerinated potato sterilisation schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: After inserting potato wedges moistened with 25% glycerine solution, sterilise tubes in the steamer at 100°C for twenty minutes on each of five consecutive days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prolonged fractional sterilisation (five days) for glycerinated potato to ensure sterility; do not shorten without justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of preservatives/dyes (fuchsin, brilliant green, malachite green, china green)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add specified dye solutions and accompanying reagents at given amounts and concentrations (e.g., fuchsin alcoholic solution 5 c.c.; brilliant green 1 per thousand aqueous solution in measured volumes; malachite green 0.1% for 'weak' and 2% additions for 'strong' medium).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare dye stock solutions per recipe (e.g., fuchsin: 3 g in 60 c.c. absolute alcohol, centrifuge and decant) and add fresh sodium sulphite or other reducing agents if specified; store some dyed media in the dark (fuchsin agar).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipes that include bile salts or sodium taurocholate
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate bile salts/sodium taurocholate at listed weights (e.g., sodium taurocholate 5 g per litre) for selective media such as bile salt agar (MacConkey) or aesculin agar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissolve and wash agar-peptone emulsions with bile salt solutions as directed; these components confer selective properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific sugar concentrations for differential media
rubrics_metrics.description: Add sugars in specified amounts (e.g., lactose 10–20 g per litre, dextrose 10 g, glucose 10 g) when preparing differential sugar media (double sugar agar, lactose litmus media etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dissolve sugars fully; adjust pH afterwards; note which sugars and concentrations are required for the diagnostic purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fractional/serial steam sterilisation schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Sterilise certain media by fractional sterilisation: e.g., in the steamer at 100°C for twenty or thirty minutes on each of three successive days (or five for some preparations), and for some media incubate at 37°C for 48 hours between cycles to discard contaminated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact number of successive-day sterilisations called for; incubate to detect contamination after intermediate sterilisation cycles before storing the remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and handling of blood-serum media
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect serum as free from haemoglobin as possible; add reagents (e.g., 0.15% sodium hydrate for Lorrain Smith), tube, stiffen at 100°C in serum inspissator, sterilise in steam steriliser (20 minutes on three successive days), then incubate at 37°C for 48 hours to eliminate contaminated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid air bubbles when filling tubes; when small numbers of tubes are filled, exhaust them in a receiver to remove air before inspissation; store sterile remainder after eliminating contaminated tubes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding sterile biological fluids after cooling (serum/ascitic fluids)
rubrics_metrics.description: After final sterilisation cool agar to a specified temperature (commonly 42°C), then add sterile hydrocele/ascitic/pleuritic fluid (e.g., 3–5 c.c. per tube) and allow to solidify in a sloping position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add only sterile fluids and at the temperature specified to avoid denaturation; slope tubes to set surfaces suitable for cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascitic/serum fluid handling and sterilisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect ascitic or pleuritic fluid aseptically, mix with sterile nutrient bouillon (often two volumes of bouillon to one of serum), filter if necessary, and sterilise by heating at 56°C for half an hour on each of five consecutive days for ascitic bouillon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use porcelain filter candles when needed; incubate after fractional heating to discard contaminated tubes and store remainder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal tissue media preparation and aseptic technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Under strict aseptic precautions remove organs from a freshly killed animal, cut into small sterile blocks, soak in sterile glycerine solution (6% in normal saline) for one hour, insert a block into sterile tubes containing glycerine bouillon, sterilise in autoclave at 120°C for thirty minutes, cap and store in ice chest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sterile instruments, sterile glass tubing supports in tubes, and ensure thorough sterilisation; tissues from postmortems may be used after prior sterilisation by boiling or autoclaving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Egg-based media preparation and inspissation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare egg albumen or whole-egg mixtures with distilled water and NaOH (0.15% NaOH), filter, tube, then stiffen at 100°C in serum inspissator; incubate at 37°C for 48 hours and discard contaminated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional addition of glucose 1–2% is permitted; where eggs are treated with caustic soda for certain methods, follow the extended processing steps (e.g., ten days in NaOH then slicing and sterilising).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blood agar preparation using fresh animal blood
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare nutrient agar slants, evaporate condensation, obtain fresh blood aseptically from a recently killed animal (sear heart surface, collect blood), apply blood to slanted agar surface to coagulate and set, then incubate and eliminate contaminated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sterilise instruments and moisten hair with disinfectant (2% lysol) before opening; allow blood to coagulate on slants and incubate 48 hours to check sterility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incubator temperature standards and required units
rubrics_metrics.description: Laboratory should have at least two incubators: a 'hot' incubator at 37°C for fluid media and most solid media, and a 'cool' incubator at 20–22°C for gelatine-solid media; additional incubators at 42°C and 60°C are useful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain constant temperature using thermostatic regulators; ensure separate incubators for temperature-specific studies (psychrophiles, yeasts, moulds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermo-regulator necessity and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Thermo-regulators are essential for maintaining constant incubator temperatures; commonly used types include Reichert's (mercury bulb regulator) and Hearson's capsule (sealed capsule with liquid boiling at desired temperature) regulators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand operation: Reichert's uses mercury expansion to control gas flow; Hearson's uses a boiling liquid capsule transmitting motion to a gas valve; both include adjustment screws/weights to set temperature and small pilot gas flow to prevent flame extinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivation methods classification (tube, plate, hanging-drop)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultivations are usually prepared as tube cultures, plate cultures, or hanging-drop cultures and incubated aerobically or anaerobically depending on organism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose method and incubation atmosphere appropriate to organism (e.g., anaerobic conditions for obligate anaerobes or certain spirochaetes).

rubrics_metrics.name: General incubation temperature rule by medium solidity
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general rule, media solidified by gelatine are incubated at ~20°C (not exceeding 22°C) while fluid media and other solid media are incubated at 37°C; exceptions exist for psychrophilic bacteria, yeasts, and moulds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply exceptions when studying cold-loving organisms; always confirm organism-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tube cultivation aseptic technique for fluid media
rubrics_metrics.description: Flame cotton-wool plugs of source and sterile tubes, sterilise platinum loop, avoid touching tube sides, withdraw a small portion of growth with cooled loop, emulsify in sterile bouillon, replug, sterilise loop, label with organism and date, then incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold tubes nearly horizontal and avoid capillary contamination; always cool the loop before touching medium; label immediately after inoculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solid media forms: oblique (slant) vs straight tube usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Oblique/slanted tubes (slants) present extensive surface area for 'streak' or 'smear' cultivations; straight tubes create a cylindrical medium for 'stab' or 'stick' cultivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slant gelatine and agar fresh before use; choose tube form according to intended inoculation technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streak, smear, stab and shake culture techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use flaming and sterilisation of loops/needles; for streak culture draw inoculum along centre of surface terminating near mouth; for smear culture rub over surface; for stab culture thrust needle deeply along axis; for shake culture liquefy medium, inoculate, allow to set upright and incubate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replug and sterilise instruments after use; label tubes; for stab cultures ensure medium surface is even (re-liquefy and reset if concave).

rubrics_metrics.name: Esmarch's roll cultivation technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquefy three gelatine tubes, prepare dilutions as for plates, roll tubes on an ice block (or under cold water) until gelatine sets as a thin film on inner surface to create a rolled cultivation; agar for roll should include 1% gelatine or 1% agar to ensure adhesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hold tubes almost horizontally while rolling; use appropriate dilution steps analogous to plate methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tissue medium method for anaerobic spirochaetes
rubrics_metrics.description: Place a sterile piece of animal tissue in each sterile tube, pour ascitic agar (nutrient agar + ascitic fluid) into tubes, allow to set, overlay with sterile paraffin oil to 3 cm depth to maintain anaerobiosis, incubate at 37°C and discard contaminated tubes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use anaerobic conditions (paraffin oil) and aseptic technique; incubate several days and only store sterile tubes for future use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator reactions and diagnostic colony appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Some media are diagnostic by colour changes or colony appearance (e.g., aesculin agar: B. coli and allied organisms give black colonies surrounded by black halo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare ferric/aesculin components as specified (aesculin 1.0 g, ferric citrate 0.5 g) and interpret colony pigmentation/halo as a diagnostic sign.
